questions.q: What's the fastest way to open the Incident table's list view without browsing the Application Navigator tree?
options: Type "incident.list" into the Application Navigator's filter box and press Enter
Open System Properties and search for "incident"
There is no faster way than expanding the Incident application manually
Type "incident.do" to open the list view
questions.explain: The <table>.list direct-navigation shortcut opens the list view immediately, with no module required.

questions.q: In the lab, which field and operator build the condition that filters incidents to the Network group?
options: Short description contains "Network"
Assignment group is Network
Caller is Network
Category is Network
questions.explain: The condition builder sets Assignment group to "is" Network to narrow the list to that group's incidents.

questions.q: What UI element opens the condition builder on a list view?
options: The user's profile picture in the header
The filter icon (a funnel) near the breadcrumb above the column headers
The Application Navigator's History tab
The gear icon in the header
questions.explain: The funnel-shaped filter icon above the list's column headers opens the condition builder.

questions.q: Where should the lab's new admin go to check their personal time zone preference?
options: The System Properties application
Their own profile picture or avatar menu in the top-right corner
The Incident table's condition builder
The Application Navigator's Favorites tab
questions.explain: Personal time zone is a per-user preference, reachable from the user's own profile/avatar menu, never from System Properties.

questions.q: Why does the lab say the admin would never look for their time zone setting in System Properties?
options: Because System Properties doesn't exist on developer instances
Because time zone is a personal preference belonging only to that user, not an instance-wide setting
Because System Properties only controls incident records
Because time zone can only be set by an administrator for every user at once
questions.explain: Personal preferences like time zone apply to one user only — exactly the distinction drawn in Lesson 8 between system settings and personal preferences.
